title: Escape from 100 Million B.C. - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cpd3lbm5tL8

Daniel (@dungeondive) champions Escape from 100 Million B.C., a Kevin Wilson design from IDW that is out of print yet sells used for about $20. A time machine has crashed on a volcano's lip, stranding a team of scientists in the deep past. Players hex-crawl a growing tile map, gather cargo crates and time machine parts, dodge or fight dinosaurs, and round up historical castaways who have fallen through rift portals, all while a paradox track creeps toward eruption. Four things earn his praise. The game generates wacky, serendipitous moments: in his current session the Big Lebowski, Albert Einstein and a mysterious death ray are floating together in the ocean. Tile barriers create genuine maze-like navigation, rare in hex crawls. Castaways make threat management dynamic because they wander randomly and get eaten by dinosaurs, and escorting them home lowers paradox. Loot doubles as a threat system, since every undiscovered item adds paradox at the end depending on how anachronistic it is. Two things drag it down: dreadful clip-art tile artwork unworthy of the designer or publisher, and a rulebook so muddled it needs a seven-page FAQ and makes a breezy game feel fiddly. He recommends grabbing a BGG rules summary and wishes the non-combat encounter deck were twice as thick and the dinosaur decks half as deep.

----

Daniel calls the loot-as-paradox scoring something he has never seen elsewhere. What other game makes the stuff you did not find matter as much as what you did?
